tasks.title: MASTER-073: ObjectKind gains a None member at zero, and the single construction chokepoint rejects it
acceptance: THE MEMBER: `src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/ObjectKind.cs` gains a member named `None` declared FIRST, above the existing `// ── Doors (wall-snap)` group comment, written as a bare `None,` with NO explicit numeric value, and carrying an XML doc comment stating that it means no kind has been specified and is never a legal kind for a `PlacedObject`. No explicit numeric value is introduced anywhere in the file — `grep -nE "= *[0-9]" src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/ObjectKind.cs` returns nothing. The five group comments are preserved and no existing member is renamed, reordered or removed. Per contracts/core-type-identity.md §1.1.

THE COUNT: after the edit `grep -cE "^[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*," src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/ObjectKind.cs` prints 38, where it printed 37 before. Record both numbers. Use that CRLF-safe form: tracked files are CRLF, so the `$`-anchored form returns 0 on this repository and must not be used for any count in this task.

THE DOMAIN GUARD, TWO CONDITIONS IN ONE GUARD: `src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/PlacedObject.cs`'s five-parameter `internal PlacedObject(Guid floorId, ObjectKind kind, CanvasPoint position, ObjectRotation rotation, float scale)` keeps its signature, parameter names and order unchanged and rejects BOTH `kind == ObjectKind.None` AND a `kind` that is not a defined member of `ObjectKind`, each with an exactly-typed `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` carrying ParamName `kind` and the offending value as `ActualValue`, per contracts/core-type-identity.md §2.1. Both conditions are required: `Enum.IsDefined(ObjectKind.None)` is `true`, so the defined-member test does not imply the `None` test, and the `None` test does not cover a cast from a numeric value. The whole guard runs textually BEFORE the existing `scale` rejection and before the first field assignment.

THE GUARD IS NOT DUPLICATED AND NOT WIDENED: the four-parameter overload is NOT separately guarded — it delegates to the five-parameter one, so one guard covers both. The `private PlacedObject()` constructor stays ungated (EF materialises through it). `src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floors/FloorObjectMethods.cs` is not edited — it is the constructor's only caller, which is what makes this a single chokepoint. `src/DungeonMaster.App/Assets/ObjectAssets/ObjectKindInfo.cs` is NOT edited: its `_ =>` arms absorbing `None` is a named, accepted residual (contracts/core-type-identity.md §2.4), carried to the Gate 3 backlog. `UpdatePlacedObjectCommandValidator.cs` is not edited — its command carries no `Kind`. If the task concludes any of these is genuinely entailed, it stops and escalates.

THE VALIDATOR RULE: `src/DungeonMaster.Application/Features/Dungeons/Commands/AddPlacedObject/AddPlacedObjectCommandValidator.cs` keeps its existing `RuleFor(command => command.Kind).IsInEnum()` at `:25-27` and adds a `.NotEqual(ObjectKind.None)` rule to the same property, per contracts/core-type-identity.md §2.2. Both rules are required, because `IsInEnum()` is `Enum.IsDefined` underneath and `None` is a defined member. No other rule in the file is changed.

REJECTION TESTS DISCRIMINATE BY ParamName, NOT BY TYPE: this same constructor already throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for an out-of-range `scale`, so a test asserting only the exception type could pass for the wrong reason (contracts/core-type-identity.md §2.3, trap 1). Every rejection test asserts `ThrowExactly<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>()`, asserts `.Which.ParamName` is `kind`, and asserts `.Which.ActualValue` is the value passed in. The `None` case and the undefined-cast case each get their own rejection test, because a suite covering only one would pass against a guard missing the other (trap 2).

NEW DOMAIN TEST FILE, EXACT SHAPE: a new file `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Domain/Entities/Floor/ObjectKindGuardTests.cs` containing exactly 8 `[Fact]` methods and no `[Theory]`, so the count is unambiguous: (1) `(int)ObjectKind.None` is 0 and `default(ObjectKind)` is `ObjectKind.None`; (2) `(int)ObjectKind.DoorWood` is 1 and `(int)ObjectKind.DoorIron` is 2, proving declaration order survived; (3) `Enum.GetValues<ObjectKind>()` has 38 entries and exactly one casts to 0, and it is `None`; (4) `Enum.IsDefined(ObjectKind.None)` is TRUE — this fact exists to record, in a test rather than in prose, why the guard needs its own `None` condition and why the validator needs `.NotEqual`; (5) the four-parameter constructor rejects `ObjectKind.None`; (6) the five-parameter constructor rejects `(ObjectKind)999`; (7) ORDERING — a call bad in BOTH `kind` and `scale` throws with ParamName `kind`, proving the guard precedes the scale rejection; (8) POSITIVE CONTROL — the constructor accepts `ObjectKind.DoorWood` with a valid scale and sets `Kind`, `FloorId`, `Position` and `Rotation`. After the edit `grep -c "\[Fact\]" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Domain/Entities/Floor/ObjectKindGuardTests.cs` prints 8. The file's namespace is `DungeonMaster.Tests.Domain.Entities.Floor`, which shadows the type name `Floor`; the sibling `PlacedObjectTests.cs` in the same folder shows the working `using` set for this shape.

VALIDATOR TESTS, 7 TO 9, INCLUDING THE ONE THAT RECORDS WHY THE SECOND RULE EXISTS: `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Validators/AddPlacedObjectCommandValidatorTests.cs` gains exactly 2 new `[Fact]` methods. (a) The production `AddPlacedObjectCommandValidator` rejects a command whose `Kind` is `ObjectKind.None` and whose every other field is valid, with `result.IsValid` false and `result.Errors` containing a single error whose `PropertyName` is `nameof(AddPlacedObjectCommand.Kind)`; model it on the existing `Validate_WithRotationOutsideTheEnum_ReturnsViolation`. (b) A validator carrying ONLY `RuleFor(command => command.Kind).IsInEnum()` ACCEPTS a command whose `Kind` is `ObjectKind.None` — this is the fact that proves `.NotEqual(ObjectKind.None)` is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces. Construct that throwaway validator however FluentValidation in this repository allows (an `InlineValidator<AddPlacedObjectCommand>`, or a private nested `AbstractValidator<AddPlacedObjectCommand>` in the test file); if neither is available, report that and fall back to asserting `Enum.IsDefined(ObjectKind.None)` is true, stating in the report which route was used and why. After the edit `grep -c "\[Fact\]" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Application/Features/Dungeons/Validators/AddPlacedObjectCommandValidatorTests.cs` prints 9 (it printed 7 before; record both).

DISCRIMINATION, RUN NOT ASSERTED, TWO SEPARATE INJECTIONS: (a) delete the `.NotEqual(ObjectKind.None)` rule from `AddPlacedObjectCommandValidator.cs`, leaving everything else in place, run `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ObjectKindGuardTests|FullyQualifiedName~AddPlacedObjectCommandValidatorTests"`, and record the observed result: validator fact (a) must FAIL, while validator fact (b) — the `IsInEnum`-alone fact — must stay GREEN, and all 8 `ObjectKindGuardTests` facts must stay GREEN. Fact (b) staying green while (a) fails is the whole demonstration: it shows the production validator lost a rule that `IsInEnum` never provided. (b) Restore the rule, then delete the `kind` guard from `PlacedObject`, run the same command, and record that facts (5), (6) and (7) FAIL while facts (1), (2), (3), (4) and (8) and both validator facts stay GREEN. Restore and re-run to green. The report names the command and quotes the failure lines for both injections. A red-step-first order satisfies either half equally; what is required is that the failure was observed and that in each injection a named control stayed green. No third injection is specified for removing the `None` member itself — that is a compile failure, not a test failure, and a build error is not discrimination evidence.

NO STORED None: `ObjectKind.None` is persistable as the string "None" under the existing `HasConversion<string>()` mapping, which it was not before this change, so no datum may carry it. After the edits, `grep -rn --include=*.cs "ObjectKind.None" src/`, with `/obj/` and `/bin/` filtered, returns hits ONLY inside this task's five owned files; and `grep -rnF --include=*.json '"None"' src/`, with `/obj/` and `/bin/` filtered, returns nothing. Report both outputs. No seed, fixture, test scene or asset-pack manifest stores `None` as a `Kind`.

FULL SOLUTION BUILD: `dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln` reports 0 warnings and 0 errors across all three App target frameworks. `ObjectKind` is consumed by `src/DungeonMaster.App` (`ObjectKindInfo`, `ObjectAssetCatalogue`, `ObjectPackRegistry`, `FloorMapDrawable`, the palette views), so building only the Tests project would not prove the new member compiles everywhere. Close any running `DungeonMaster.App` first or the Windows TFM fails with MSB3026/MSB3027. `IDE0055` is a build error in this repository, so a formatting slip fails here. Do not add `src/DungeonMaster.App.UiTests` to the solution.

SUITE, MEASURED BY THIS TASK AGAINST ITS OWN BASELINE: before making any edit, run all three test projects in `src/DungeonMaster.sln` and record each project's passing count. After the edits, run them again. Required: 0 failed in all three; `DungeonMaster.Tests` up by exactly 10 (8 new domain facts + 2 new validator facts); `DungeonMaster.App.Tests` and `DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests` unchanged. Report all six numbers. Do NOT compare against a total quoted from a previous session — this task measures its own baseline. If a count moves other than as stated, report the discrepancy with the actual output rather than adjusting a test to reach it.

PACK AND PERSISTENCE UNAFFECTED, PROVEN BY THE SUITE NOT BY ASSERTION: `PlacedObjectConfiguration` maps `Kind` with `HasConversion<string>()` and `ObjectPackRegistry`/`FakeAssetSource` parse by name, so the ordinal shift is invisible to both (contracts/core-type-identity.md §1.4). The evidence is that `PlacedObjectConfigurationTests` and every test under `src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/Graphics/` pass unmodified. Do not edit `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/**` or any asset-pack `pack.json`; if either turns out to need a change, stop and escalate — that would refute the measurement and CORE-017's migration clause would have been right after all.

NO STRAY EDITS: no file outside this task's `owns` globs is created or modified. Every edit is made through the edit tools; `sed -i` is never used on a tracked file. This task's tests must not assert equality or inequality between two `PlacedObject` instances, and must not use `Contains`, `Distinct` or a `HashSet<PlacedObject>` — `Entity` equality changes under T2 and contracts/core-type-identity.md §3.4 forbids depending on it here.

tasks.title: MASTER-074: Entity compares and hashes by identity
acceptance: EQUALITY MEMBERS: `src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Entity.cs` implements `IEquatable<Entity>` and overrides both `Equals(object?)` and `GetHashCode()`, per contracts/core-type-identity.md §3.1. `Id`, `CreatedAt`, `LastModified` and `protected void Touch()` keep their current declarations, accessibility and XML doc comments, and `Id` keeps its `private set`. New members carry XML doc comments in the same tab-indented style as the existing ones.

NO OPERATORS: no `==` or `!=` operator is declared on `Entity`. This is a frozen decision (contracts/core-type-identity.md §3.1) — declaring them would change the meaning of every existing `==` over an entity-typed expression in the repository, a surface this session has not measured, and CORE-018's own suggested direction names neither. `grep -n "operator ==\|operator !=" src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Entity.cs` returns nothing. If the task believes the operators are entailed, it stops and escalates.

BEHAVIOUR TABLE: every row of contracts/core-type-identity.md §3.2 holds, for BOTH the `IEquatable<Entity>` overload and the `Equals(object?)` overload — reference-equal is true; same runtime type with the same `Id` is true and the two hash codes are equal; same runtime type with different `Id` is false; different runtime types (an `Area` and a `Floor`) sharing an `Id` is false; `null` is false. Runtime type participates via `GetType()`, not via a pattern match on a named type.

HASH STABILITY: `GetHashCode()` is derived from `Id`, optionally combined with the runtime type, and incorporates NO mutable state — not `CreatedAt`, not `LastModified`. Proven by a test that captures the hash of a floor, drives a mutation through the aggregate that calls `Touch()` so `LastModified` changes (assert that it changed, or the test is vacuous), then asserts the hash is unchanged AND that the floor still equals a distinct same-`Id` instance. Reading `LastModified` into the hash is the specific defect this test exists to catch.

THE THREE Remove SITES ARE UNTOUCHED AND STILL PASS: `DungeonMethods.cs:74`, `FloorMethods.cs:98` and `FloorObjectMethods.cs:73` are outside this task's `owns` and are not edited. Each already retrieves the instance from the same list by `Id` before removing it, so reference equality was exact there and the change must not alter their behaviour. Evidence is that every existing test under `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Domain/` passes unmodified.

EF IS UNAFFECTED: no file under `src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure/**` is edited — the change tracker keys on the primary key, not on `Equals`/`GetHashCode`. Evidence is that every existing test under `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Infrastructure/` passes unmodified, including the change-tracking and configuration tests. If any Infrastructure test needs a change, stop and escalate: that would refute contracts/core-type-identity.md §3.4.

NO PRODUCTION SEAM FOR TESTABILITY: `Id` does not become `internal set`, no test-only constructor, factory or `WithId` helper is added, and `src/DungeonMaster.Domain/AssemblyInfo.cs` is not edited. Two distinct instances sharing an `Id` are produced by reflection on the declaring type's property, `typeof(Entity).GetProperty(nameof(Entity.Id))!.SetValue(instance, someGuid)` — verified working on SDK 10.0.400 against an equivalent shape and recorded in contracts/core-type-identity.md §3.5, so it is not a guess. If it does not work here, stop and escalate rather than adding a seam.

NEW TEST FILE, EXACT SHAPE, CONTROLS LABELLED: a new file `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Domain/Entities/EntityEqualityTests.cs` containing exactly 8 `[Fact]` methods and no `[Theory]`, so the count is unambiguous. DISCRIMINATING (these fail against today's code): (1) two distinct `Floor` instances with the same `Id` are equal through the typed overload; (2) the same through `Equals(object?)`; (3) their `GetHashCode()` values are equal; (4) `dungeon.Floors.Contains(clone)` is true, where `clone` is a distinct `Floor` carrying the `Id` of a floor added through `dungeon.AddFloor` — this is the observable effect at the real `List<T>` surface the measurement named, and it is the criterion that connects the type change to the three `Remove` sites. CONTROLS (these already pass against today's reference equality and prove nothing on their own — contracts/core-type-identity.md §3.6): (5) two `Floor` instances with different `Id` are not equal; (6) an `Area` and a `Floor` forced to the same `Id` are not equal; (7) `x.Equals(null)` is false and `x.Equals(x)` is true. Plus (8) the hash-stability test above. Each test's XML doc comment or a one-line comment states whether it is discriminating or a control. After the edit `grep -c "\[Fact\]" src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Domain/Entities/EntityEqualityTests.cs` prints 8.

NAMESPACE SHADOWING: the new file sits in namespace `DungeonMaster.Tests.Domain.Entities`, which contains the child namespaces `.Area`, `.Dungeon` and `.Floor` from the sibling folders, so a bare `Floor`, `Area` or `Dungeon` binds to a namespace and the file will not compile. Alias the domain types (for example `using DomainFloor = DungeonMaster.Domain.Entities.Floors.Floor;`), as `src/DungeonMaster.Tests/Domain/Entities/Floor/` already aliases `Dungeon`. The `Floor` constructor is internal and, since MASTER-169, rejects a number below 1 — construct with `1` or higher, or obtain the floor from `dungeon.AddFloor(name)`.

DISCRIMINATION, RUN NOT ASSERTED: after the tests pass, delete the `Equals(Entity?)`, `Equals(object?)` and `GetHashCode()` overrides from `Entity.cs` (leaving `IEquatable<Entity>` off too, so the file still compiles), run `dotnet test src/DungeonMaster.Tests/DungeonMaster.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~EntityEqualityTests"`, and record the observed result: facts (1), (2), (3) and (4) must FAIL while the three controls (5), (6), (7) must still PASS. The controls staying green is what proves the run was not broken by something unrelated; a run in which a control also failed does not satisfy this criterion. Then restore and re-run to green. The report names the command and quotes the failure lines, and states explicitly that the evidence came from the discriminating facts and not from the controls.

FULL SOLUTION BUILD: `dotnet build src/DungeonMaster.sln` reports 0 warnings and 0 errors across all three App target frameworks. `AnalysisMode` is `Recommended` at `AnalysisLevel` 10.0 with `TreatWarningsAsErrors`, so an equality override that trips CA1067, CA2218, CA2224, CS0659 or CS0661 fails the build rather than warning. Close any running `DungeonMaster.App` first or the Windows TFM fails with MSB3026/MSB3027.

SUITE, MEASURED BY THIS TASK AGAINST ITS OWN BASELINE: before making any edit — that is, with T1 already landed in the worktree — run all three test projects in `src/DungeonMaster.sln` and record each project's passing count. After the edits, run them again. Required: 0 failed in all three; `DungeonMaster.Tests` up by exactly 8; `DungeonMaster.App.Tests` and `DungeonMaster.App.UnitTests` unchanged. Report all six numbers. If a count moves other than as stated, report the discrepancy with the actual output rather than adjusting a test to reach it.

NO STRAY EDITS: no file outside this task's `owns` globs is created or modified. No subclass of `Entity` (`Area`, `Dungeon`, `Floor`, `PlacedObject`) gains its own equality override — the base class is the whole of the change. Every edit is made through the edit tools; `sed -i` is never used on a tracked file.
